paper: The Short-Term Effects of Generative AI on Employment: Evidence from an Online Labor Market
what_it_shows: After ChatGPT's release, freelancers in more-exposed Upwork occupations had fewer monthly jobs and lower earnings than less-exposed occupations. The cleanest displacement result in the stack, in the narrowest market.

paper: Who is AI Replacing? The Impact of Generative AI on Online Freelancing Platforms
what_it_shows: Freelance demand fell sharply in writing and graphic-design categories after image and text models launched; the decline is concentrated in exactly the tasks models do well.

paper: Artificial Intelligence and the Labor Market
what_it_shows: Firm-level AI investment is associated with weaker hiring, with the burden falling on entry-level and lower-skill roles rather than on total headcount.

paper: AI exposure predicts unemployment risk: A new approach to technology-driven job loss
what_it_shows: Exposure scores carry information about unemployment risk, though individual scores alone are weak predictors. Best read as evidence that exposure is not noise.

paper: Automation and New Tasks: How Technology Displaces and Reinstates Labor
what_it_shows: Why displacement claims must be paired with reinstatement. The negative case has to survive this frame, not ignore it.

paper: Artificial Intelligence and Jobs: Evidence from Online Vacancies
what_it_shows: AI-exposed establishments post more AI vacancies without clear total employment declines — the strongest counterweight to the freelancer results.

paper: Rethinking Automation Risk: AI Applicability and Occupational Outcomes, 2019-24
what_it_shows: Occupations with higher AI applicability saw employment and wages grow over 2019-24. Directly contradicts the displacement thesis at the occupation level.

paper: GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models
what_it_shows: The exposure index everything else is built on. Capability overlap, not adoption — treat it as a hypothesis generator.
